analysis.title: Wall Street is crowded, confused and caught offside
key_insights: Mag 7 implied volatility trades at a discount to the broader tech complex. The relative vol ratio is at the 15th percentile over four years (GS).
The NDX/SPX implied vol spread compressed sharply after last week's blowout. The three-day compression was the largest in four years, but the 1-month ATM spread is still at the 94th percentile (GS).
Long/short hedge funds' rolling Mag 7 beta is near the 97th percentile historically. Mutual fund beta is near the 11th percentile (Nomura, McElligott).
Goldman Prime data show fundamental long/short momentum exposure fell from nearly 70% at the peak to around 15%.
Korean equities trade at record-low forward P/E multiples. Excluding the memory giants, KOSPI trades at 8.4x forward earnings, the 11th percentile historically (JPM, note of October 20).
Korea RSI fell to its lowest level since Liberation Day and the number of oversold stocks reached extreme levels (JPM).
Net allocation to Korea fell to 3.4% (29th percentile over one year, 86th over five years). Gross allocation fell to 2.4% (30th percentile over one year, 86th over five years) (GS).
US homebuilder operating margins have fallen below pre-Covid levels as weaker new-home prices meet rising construction, labor and financing costs (TS Lombard).
Mortgage rates are around 7.3% and affordability remains near historically depressed levels. TS Lombard warns a more hawkish Fed could add upward pressure to rates and further hurt housing demand.
Brazil's debt-to-GDP ratio has risen to 81.9% from 71.7% when Lula took office in 2023. On a business-as-usual path debt could reach almost 118% of GDP by 2036 (TS Lombard).
TS Lombard warns that without fiscal reform Brazil could face a partial government shutdown in 2028, as mandatory spending crowds out discretionary spending.

sector_views.rationale: Operating margins are below pre-Covid levels as weaker new-home prices collide with higher construction, labor and financing costs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Affordability stays depressed, and a more hawkish Fed could push rates higher and weaken housing demand further.
Up from 71.7% in 2023, which raises doubts about Brazil's debt stabilization.

risk_factors: A more hawkish Fed could lift mortgage rates and further hurt US housing demand.
Brazil's fiscal trajectory could force an adjustment through arithmetic, including a possible partial government shutdown in 2028.
Hedge fund crowding in the Mag 7 leaves positioning exposed against underweight mutual funds.
vol_and_positioning: Mag 7 implied vol relative to tech is at the 15th percentile over four years, so Mag 7 options look cheap versus the rest of tech (GS).
The NDX/SPX 1-month ATM implied vol spread is at the 94th percentile after the largest three-day compression in four years (GS).
Long/short hedge fund rolling Mag 7 beta is near the 97th percentile, while mutual fund beta is near the 11th percentile (Nomura).
Fundamental long/short momentum exposure fell from nearly 70% to around 15% (GS Prime).
Net allocation to Korea is 3.4% and gross allocation is 2.4%, both low versus five-year history (GS).
geopolitical: Lula won another term in Brazil, and fiscal sustainability is now the key question for investors.
